cases.rationale: The question explicitly asks to walk the hierarchy chain up from CAPEC-606 through its parents to the most abstract pattern. The gate query correctly retrieved the full chain: CAPEC-606 -> CAPEC-620 (Drop Encryption Level, role=standard) -> CAPEC-212 (Functionality Misuse, role=meta), visible in the record's 'related' array in logic_flow. However, the answer's narrative and claims only report CAPEC-606's own Abstraction/Status properties and never mention CAPEC-620 or CAPEC-212 at all, despite both being present in evidence and required by gold.must_include_related. This is not a hallucination (nothing false is stated, so faithfulness/groundedness are high) but it is a correctness failure: the answer does not perform the hierarchy walk the analyst asked for, even though the pipeline had all the necessary data in hand. deterministic_scores.coverage confirms this internally (found 1/3, missing CAPEC-212 and CAPEC-620). Verdict is INCORRECT because the core ask of the question goes unanswered despite full evidence availability.

Gold requires two CAPEC attack patterns linked to CWE-1243 (must_include_ids: CAPEC-116, CAPEC-545), but the executed cwe_chain query (logic_flow results[0]) only returned CAPEC-545 (row_count 2, normalized to 1 record with join_values T1005/T1555.001) -- CAPEC-116 (Excavation) is absent from evidence entirely, so the answer's claim 'Found 1 CAPEC record(s) for CAPEC-545' materially understates the true set and the question 'what attack patterns are linked to CWE-1243' is only half-answered. Everything the answer does assert is faithful and grounded: CAPEC-545's CWE-1243 relation, its ATT&CK mappings (T1005, T1555.001), the mitigations (M1027 for T1555.001, M1057 for T1005) and the two cross-source correlations (T1005, T1555.001) all match logic_flow verbatim -- no invented ids, names, or dates. must_correlate (T1005, T1555.001), attack.must_include_ids and attack.must_include_related are fully satisfied (8/9 gold sub-items), but the missing CAPEC-116 is a genuine retrieval gap, not merely a display omission, so this is PARTIAL rather than CORRECT.

The abstention itself was procedurally clean: the system made no claims, fabricated no CAPEC-to-ATT&CK correlation, and both the capec query and the attack dependency-skip reason are carried verbatim in the abstentions block, so an analyst can see exactly what was searched (g.V().hasLabel("Weakness").has("id",within(cweIds))...out("MAPS_TO")...taxonomy_name==ATTACK). However, gold.assertions is not a blanket 'expect nothing' case: gold.capec specifies min_records=1 and must_include_ids=[CAPEC-456, CAPEC-679], meaning CWE-1316 does have known exploiting attack patterns that a correct answer should surface for the first half of the question ('which attack patterns exploit CWE-1316'). gold.expect_no_correlation/must_correlate=[] and attack.expect_dependency_skip apply to the second half (CAPEC->ATT&CK technique mapping / downstream mitigations), which legitimately has no live mapping and was correctly skipped. The system's single chained Gremlin query joined Weakness->AttackPattern->MAPS_TO->ATTACK TaxonomyEntry as one non-optional traversal, so when the MAPS_TO(ATTACK) hop found nothing, it silently discarded the CAPEC-456/CAPEC-679 matches too (row_count=0 at the 'execute' step), rather than surfacing the known attack patterns and only abstaining on the ATT&CK correlation. This is a retrieval/query-design gap, not a fabrication: nothing false was asserted, but 2 of 2 gold-required CAPEC records were missed, so completeness=0 and correctness is low despite the honest, well-proofed empty response.

hallucinations: Narrative states 'T1583 (Acquire Infrastructure) has 1 related item(s): T1583.003', implicitly answering the question's second half ('does that parent have other sub-techniques alongside it?') as 'no'. But the executed Cypher query filters WHERE t.attack_id IN $ids OR st.attack_id IN $ids with $ids=['T1583.003'] -- since parent ids never match a sub-technique seed, this can only ever return the single row matching st.attack_id='T1583.003'. The query is structurally incapable of surfacing sibling sub-techniques of T1583 even if they exist, so the '1 related item(s)' count is not evidence that T1583.003 is the only sub-technique of T1583; it is an artifact of the seed-restricted query.
cases.rationale: Gold assertions (must_include_ids: T1583.003, must_include_related: T1583, min_records 1) are fully satisfied: the answer correctly names T1583 (Acquire Infrastructure) as the parent of T1583.003 (Virtual Private Server), both ids traceable to logic_flow.records[0] (primary_id T1583, related[0].id T1583.003). Coverage per deterministic_scores is 1.0/1.0 and citations are fully provenanced. However, the question explicitly asks a second question -- whether T1583 has other sub-techniques alongside T1583.003 -- and the narrative's phrasing ('has 1 related item(s)') reads as an implicit 'no', which is not actually grounded: the query was seeded on T1583.003 only and structurally cannot retrieve or rule out sibling sub-techniques (e.g. T1583.001 Domains, T1583.002 DNS Server, T1583.004 Server, T1583.005 Botnet, T1583.006 Web Services, all real MITRE ATT&CK v19 sub-techniques of T1583 that this query never had the ability to see). Since gold's ex_gold pool only expects T1583 as a neighbor and does not test sibling completeness, this doesn't sink coverage, but it does mean half of what the analyst literally asked was answered by a query artifact rather than genuine evidence -- a real but minor unsupported implication, not a fabricated fact-name/count. Hence PARTIAL rather than CORRECT.
